subject: MarketPulse — follow-up: performance targets, streaming, and token limits
messages:

Subject: MarketPulse — follow-up: performance targets, streaming, and token limits

Hi Kai / Lina,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good discussion. Quick recap + a few clarifying questions so our SRE/solutions teams can size a small POC:

What we heard as top priorities (please confirm):
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile response time target for user-facing requests
- Streaming: incremental tokens are displayed to end users as they arrive (real-time streaming)
- Context window: variable between short (<=512 tokens) and long (up to ~8k) depending on feature flags
- Concurrency: bursts of ~120 concurrent end-user requests during peak campaign windows
- Throughput: sustained background batch processing for analytics (non-streaming) ~100 reqs/min

Open questions for you:
1) Can you confirm the most common prompt sizes for the two main flows? (a) search-assist short prompts + 150 tokens output, (b) summarization long-context up to 6k input, ~800 token output
2) Which interactions must be streamed vs acceptable to return as a single response?
3) Any regional constraints on data residency or single-region routing?

If the above is accurate, our recommended next steps:
- Lauren will sketch two POC profiles (interactive streaming profile + batch summarization profile) and provide estimated latencies and GPU sizing.
- We’ll run a 2-week POC with priority telemetry (95/99 p95/p99, per-token cost, end-to-end render times)
- Share SLO/contract expectations and any required audit/compliance docs.

Attach: the short SLO worksheet you can fill (slo_requirements.xlsx). Also recording attached.

Thanks,

— Sergio

Subject: Re: MarketPulse — follow-up: performance targets, streaming, and token limits

Thanks Sergio — great walkthrough. Short answers to your open questions: 

1) Prompt sizes: your guessed buckets are right for the majority. Rough split: 70% search-assist (user prompts ~40–160 tokens, outputs 80–200), 20% document summarization (inputs 2k–6k, outputs 400–900), 10% misc (short chat).

2) Streaming: search-assist must stream (typeahead / progressive answer). Summarization can be non-streaming; incremental progress display is nice-to-have but not required for v1.

3) Data residency: US-only for now; we operate out of AWS us-west-2.

We’re happy to proceed with the two POC profiles. For sizing: peak concurrent active users equates to ~120 concurrent streaming sessions; average token throughput during peak ~55k tokens/min.

Also attached a short doc with expected SLA commitments from our product side — mainly 99% availability and 95th percentile response targets for interactive flows.

— Kai
Kai Sullivan
Head of Platform — MarketPulse
kai@marketpulse.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Kai Sullivan <kai@marketpulse.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MarketPulse — follow-up: performance targets, streaming, and token limits

Hi Kai / team — looping in some technical detail so expectations are concrete. High level tradeoffs and realistic estimates based on our runtime: 

TL;DR recommended profiles:
- Interactive streaming profile (for search-assist): optimize for low tail latency; recommend model variants quantized int8, persistent KV cache for short prompts, 95% target <= 250ms for first token, 95% token-step latency <= 40ms for subsequent tokens at 512-token context. Estimated GPU sizing: 2x A100 equivalent nodes per 60 concurrent streaming sessions (w/ moderate batching).
- Summarization batch profile (long context): prefer chunk+rerank or sliding-window context; latent throughput per request grows roughly linearly with input tokens. For a 6k input -> 800 token output on an A100: expect median end-to-end ~1.2–1.6s, p95 ~2.8–4.5s depending on batching and KV reuse.

Key points / assumptions:
- Context window impact: doubling context length increases memory and KV management overhead; for autoregressive generation, per-token latency increases modestly for token-step but end-to-end increases because of more attention compute on the input side during first decode steps.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming requires keeping lower-latency scheduling and smaller micro-batches; batching improves throughput but hurts tail latency for streaming users. We can configure hybrid policies: prioritize streaming sessions into low-latency lanes and batch background summarization separately.
- Concurrency handling: 120 concurrent streaming sessions is doable; we size for headroom (150 concurrent) to keep p95 targets stable.
- Cost controls: quantization and prefix caching dramatically reduce GPU memory and improve throughput for repeated prompts.

Examples (ballpark numbers):
- Model: open-encoder-7b quantized int8, context 512, streaming micro-batch 8 -> first token p95 ~180–260ms, token-step p95 ~30–50ms.
- Model: open-encoder-7b quantized int8, context 6k, non-streaming batch 4 -> end-to-end p95 ~3.2s for 6k in / 800 out.

Next steps suggested (action items):
- Kai: confirm the % of requests that must be strict streaming (we have an initial number of 70% but if that shifts we need to re-run sizing).
- MarketPulse: fill in slo_requirements.xlsx with target p95/p99 and expected monthly token volume (estimates will materially affect node counts).
- Redwood: we’ll produce two POC configs (cloud-hosted sandbox): one streaming-optimized cluster and one batch/long-context cluster. Each config will include expected p50/p95/p99, cost estimate, and recommended fallback model variants.

Attaching: rough sizing sheet (we’ll drop a populated copy to the Drive link).

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com

From: Kai Sullivan <kai@marketpulse.ai>

Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@marketpulse.ai>
Date: 2026-04-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MarketPulse — follow-up: performance targets, streaming, and token limits

Thanks Lauren — this is exactly the detail we need. A couple items before we kick off the POC: 

- We will prioritize streaming for search-assist. I confirmed with product: 65–75% of user-facing calls must be streamed.
- Attached in-line is our internal SLO doc (short) — we need p95 first-token <= 300ms for streaming interactions, and p95 end-to-end <= 4s for long-context summarization. That aligns pretty closely to your estimates; please flag if any of those are infeasible.
- We require US-only deployment and standard SOC-type controls (we’ll send a vendor security questionnaire soon).

If you can send the two POC configs and a recommended schedule (we prefer starting next Tuesday), we’ll prioritize engineering time on our side. Also please include the expected telemetry we should surface: p50/p95/p99, token counts, per-request model variant, and a simple trace id so we can correlate user sessions.

Looking forward — Lina and I will complete the SLO worksheet and upload it to your Drive link by EOD Monday.

— Kai
